questiontext.text: Which set lists the four layers used by the TCP/IP model in this lesson?

answer.text: Link, Internet, transport, application
Filesystem, process, memory, device
DNS, DHCP, SSH, HTTP
Address, route, packet, socket

questiontext.text: What is a network interface?

answer.text: A physical or logical connection through which a system sends and receives network traffic
A DNS record that stores a webpage
A port number used only by TCP
A route used only for remote networks

questiontext.text: What does ip link primarily show in this lesson?

answer.text: Network interfaces and link-related state
All DNS records cached by the system
HTTP responses from remote servers
Files stored on mounted filesystems

questiontext.text: What does ip address display?

answer.text: Addresses and prefixes assigned to network interfaces
Only currently listening TCP services
All files containing IP addresses
HTTP status codes from a website

questiontext.text: What does ip route show?

answer.text: Routing entries used to decide where packets are sent
Only the active DNS server's hostname
The number of processes using the network
The filesystem mount table

questiontext.text: What does a /24 prefix indicate in an IP address notation?

answer.text: The first 24 bits identify the network portion of the prefix
The address has 24 ports
The system has 24 active network interfaces
Every packet must travel through 24 routers

questiontext.text: What does a successful test to 127.0.0.1 primarily check?

answer.text: Local network-stack behavior on the same system
That the Internet connection and DNS both work
That every remote service is available
That a physical Wi-Fi adapter is connected

questiontext.text: When is a default route generally used?

answer.text: When no more-specific route matches the destination
Only when the destination is the loopback address
Whenever DNS returns more than one address
Only for UDP traffic

questiontext.text: A default route appears in ip route. What does that prove?

answer.text: A default routing entry is configured; it does not prove end-to-end access
The gateway and every Internet service are reachable
DNS is resolving through a public server
All firewall rules allow connections

questiontext.text: What is DNS commonly used for?

answer.text: Resolving hostnames to IP addresses and supporting related name lookups
Encrypting every file stored on a server
Assigning a process ID to each network connection
Choosing file permissions for downloaded content

questiontext.text: What does getent hosts example.com ask the system to do?

answer.text: Look up the name using the system's configured host lookup path
Open a listening socket on port 80
Change the default gateway
Download and execute the website's software

questiontext.text: On a system using systemd-resolved, what does resolvectl query NAME do?

answer.text: Queries the resolver for a name or address
Changes the system hostname permanently
Lists local TCP listeners
Captures all network packets

questiontext.text: Why might a hostname lookup succeed without a public DNS server being contacted at that moment?

answer.text: The system may use a local hosts entry, cache, or another configured lookup source
Hostnames are always embedded in Ethernet addresses
DNS is performed only by the web server
Every IP address contains its hostname in the prefix

questiontext.text: What is a transport port used for?

answer.text: Identifying an application endpoint on a host
Identifying the physical network cable
Replacing an IP route
Storing a DNS cache

questiontext.text: Which statement best describes TCP compared with UDP?

answer.text: TCP provides a connection-oriented ordered byte stream; UDP sends datagrams without those TCP guarantees
UDP always guarantees delivery and ordering; TCP does not
TCP is a DNS lookup tool; UDP is an IP address
They are both application-layer file formats

questiontext.text: What does ss -tuln display in this lesson?

answer.text: Local listening TCP and UDP sockets with numeric addresses and ports
All remote devices on the subnet
The system's route table
All domains stored by public DNS

questiontext.text: Which protocol does the echo operation in ping use?

answer.text: ICMP
HTTP
DNS
SSH

questiontext.text: Why does a failed ping not prove that a host or application service is unavailable?

answer.text: ICMP may be filtered or rate-limited even when other traffic works, and ping does not test a particular application
Ping always tests every TCP port automatically
Ping checks only the DNS cache
A failed ping means the system has no IP address

questiontext.text: What does ping -c 4 DESTINATION request?

answer.text: Send four echo requests and then stop
Send requests continuously until stopped manually
Test four TCP ports on the destination
Resolve four DNS records without sending packets

questiontext.text: What does curl -I https://example.com request?

answer.text: HTTP response headers using the HEAD method when supported
A full subnet scan for open ports
A new DNS server configuration
Execution of a downloaded program

answer.text: An HTTP server responded, but the requested resource was not found
The hostname could not be resolved
The network interface is necessarily down
The DNS server refused all requests

false

answer.text: Name resolution and the configured resolver path

The local package manager cache only
Whether the monitor is powered on

questiontext.text: Which activity matches this lesson's scope?

answer.text: Inspect local interfaces and make a few bounded checks to instructor-approved destinations
Scan every address in the classroom subnet
Try guessed ports on classmates' computers
Capture unrelated users' traffic for analysis

questiontext.text: Why should a troubleshooting report separate observations from conclusions?

answer.text: It shows what was directly measured, what is inferred, and what remains uncertain
It guarantees that every network fault has one cause

It converts a local test into proof of Internet access

answer.text: Limits how long curl waits for the transfer to ten seconds
